redeployment.reason: serveRedemption had no window-closed check: a routed issuer could race settleWindowClose with a late passed=true report after the window closed and escape a genuine default. Fixed in WorkClaim.sol (WindowClosed() revert once block.timestamp >= ct.windowTo, mirroring the same guard already on presentForRedemption), covered by two new unit tests and a new invariant (invariant_noServeSucceededAfterWindowClosed, confirmed at FOUNDRY_INVARIANT_RUNS=10000 — 640000 calls, 0 reverts across all 6 invariants) before redeploying.
redeployment.whyTheWholeTrioMovedNotJustWorkClaim: CapacityBond's constructor takes WorkClaim's own address as an immutable, precomputed via vm.computeCreateAddress before WorkClaim exists (DeployGateMarket.s.sol) — the two are mutually address-pinned at construction, so WorkClaim cannot be redeployed in isolation; ClaimRouter is pinned to CapacityBond the same way. All three redeployed together as one script run.

history.reason: P4 showed every authoring run finishing in one turn regardless of model — a capable ORCHESTRATOR has no reason to subcontract, so P5 window 1 could never show emergent delegation with gpt-5.1 still assigned. Reassigned to a weaker, cheaper, non-frontier model per the user's own stated preference (make delegation rational, not scripted), verified empirically first rather than assumed.

empiricalVerification.finding: Failed to solo the same P4-style gate-authoring job cleanly. Two real, distinct signals, both disclosed rather than only citing the parse failure: (1) the raw response was prose-wrapped with markdown fences plus a separate trailing friction JSON block, breaking the simple first-brace/last-brace parser; (2) its own attempted gate source contained a genuine bug (execSync called with an argv-array second argument — execSync takes a command string plus options, not argv like execFile/spawn). Together: real evidence of lower capability, not just a formatting quirk.
empiricalVerification.outcome: Used as the real ORCHESTRATOR model per the plan's own decision rule (fails/struggles solo -> use it, delegation is rational).

history.reason: The weak-model window (data/gate-market/runs/p5-window1-2026-09-26T07-06-28-003Z/) showed a second, more severe failure mode: on its second real turn (context now including its own first failed attempt), mistral-small-3.2-24b-instruct produced no parseable tool-call JSON at all and was removed from the run before ever facing a delegation/asset-choice decision. A weak enough model to guarantee it can't solo the job is also too weak to reliably coordinate at all — the two properties don't separate cleanly for this model. User's own correction: pair a capable model with a structural constraint instead (information asymmetry — see docs/gate-market-spec.md's own §8.3 vs the ORCHESTRATOR-specific job description in packages/gate-market-agents/src/cli/p5-window1-full-run.ts, which now withholds the technical contract/reference materials from ORCHESTRATOR's own prompt entirely, so it cannot author regardless of model capability). Multi-hop/delegation is now a required, disclosed structural property of this window, not an emergent one — but F1's own question (which asset an agent pays in when it has a real, unbiased choice) was never about whether delegation happens, so it stays a genuine, unscripted measurement.
